propositions: Multiple regression-oracle test scanners independently walk source trees and redundantly parse the same Python files, with parsing consuming 75-80% of each scan's cost and causing excessive duration in coverage gates.

A shared process-global memoized parse helper with functools.cache is introduced to allow the first scanner per xdist worker to parse a given root and all subsequent scanners to reuse the cached result.
The cached parse contract uses ast.parse(source, filename=str(path)) and strict UTF-8 decoding to ensure byte-identical results to the previous scanners' behavior.

Whole-tree AST scanners over committed src/rebar and tests trees are migrated to use the shared helper, while scanners that also scan synthetic/planted or tmp_path roots are excluded to preserve their independent parse behavior.

Migration of the three heaviest test-tree scanners reduces their execution time from 6.64s→2.89s and 5.07s→1.91s with identical pass/fail results, proving pure redundancy removal without test regression.
